newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.04 pct in dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.04 pct in dollar inflows.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.04 percent to close at 1.0508 per dollar in dollar inflows on the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
After three days of consecutive deficits in the net dollar flows, the local currency recovered some ground today due to dollar inflows, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed surplus of $40 million on Thursday.

The market is divided about the last lowering in the reais-dollar mini-band this month. Some dealers believe the Central Bank will lower the mini-band by 0.05 percent on Friday, while others expect a decline of 0.1 percent.
So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.53 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was lowered between 0.50 percent and 0.65 percent.
The current mini-band was set on Tuesday between 1.0505 and 1.0555 reais per dollar.
In the floating exchange rate market, the real dipped 0.01 percent to end at 1.0569 against the greenback.
The real dropped 0.45 percent to close at 1.105 per dollar in a virtually paralysed parallel market.

The very thin turnover in the illegal parallel market was due to instability created by an ongoing investigation into an alleged multi-million dollar fraud scheme involving state and municipal bonds, traders said.
